reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Mandatory notification center participation and railroad exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires any person installing, owning, or operating an underground facility—except a railroad regulated by the Federal Railroad Administration—to join and maintain participation in a notification center for the duration of ownership and operation.

headings.title: Notification center board composition and stakeholder directors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Establishes governance by a membership-elected board plus four board-elected voting directors from construction-industry damage-prevention stakeholders (three heavy civil/site grading/road/highway contractors and one utility/underground contractor), barring board-elected directors who work for contractors owning or operating underground facilities, and subjecting all directors to bylaws and policies.

headings.title: Participant list availability and printing and mailing fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires the notification center to maintain and make available upon request to participants or excavators a current list of participant names, addresses, and counties with underground facilities, and permits a reasonable fee to recover actual printing and mailing costs. Independent review revised title from 'Participant list availability and copying fees' to match statutory wording authorizing recovery of 'actual costs of printing and mailing.'

headings.title: Informing excavators of participant list availability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires that excavators be informed of the availability of the list of notification center participants.

headings.title: Annual CPA audit or review and legislative report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires an annual CPA audit or review of the notification center with findings submitted to the house speaker and senate president pro tem.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.022:57363 (all 5 subsections and L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all source and subsection SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified FRA-regulated railroad exception, 4 stakeholder director restrictions, and annual CPA audit/review; revised subsection 3 to match 'printing and mailing' costs and retained subsections 1–2 and 4–5.

headings.title: Owner assistance and outreach on locating underground facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires underground facility owners/operators to assist excavators and the public in determining facility locations before excavation or as required under §§ 319.026(7) or 319.030(1) after excavation starts, lists permissive outreach methods, and deems notification-center information provided on an owner's behalf compliant.

headings.title: Additional identification and notice duties for pipeline operators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(3), and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Adds three duties for underground pipeline facility owners/operators: identifying regular local excavators (with annual notification-center compliance option), including § 319.025(1) notification-center information in Missouri PSC damage-prevention notices, and annually notifying notice-giving excavators of marking types and identification.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.024:57364 (both subsections, subdivisions (1)–(3), and L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified §§ 319.026(7), 319.030(1), and 319.025(1) cross-references and notification-center compliance options; retained both accurate titles.

headings.title: Pre-excavation notice, exceptions, and twenty-one-day duration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 4 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Bars starting excavation on public or private property—except under §§ 319.030(4) and 319.050—until giving § 319.026-compliant notice to the notification center and obtaining location information from listed participants, deems center notice effective as to all owners/operators, and sets an operational life ending at 11:59 p.m. 21 consecutive calendar days from the start date of work.

headings.title: Direct notice to participating owners ineffective
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Provides that an excavator's notice to owners or operators participating under section 319.022 is ineffective for subsection 1 unless given to the notification center.

headings.title: Relief from direct-notice response and listed exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Relieves notification center participants from responding to direct excavation notices, except for on-site marking-clarification meeting requests under section 319.030(1) and emergency locate requests under section 319.050.

headings.title: State highway excavation permit and railroad exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Prohibits excavating in a state highway or its right-of-way without first obtaining a highways and transportation commission permit under section 227.240, while exempting railroad-owned or railroad-operated right-of-way.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.025:57365 (all 4 subsections and L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 4 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified §§ 319.030(4)/319.050 exceptions, 21-day operational life ending 11:59 p.m., direct-notice relief exceptions, and § 227.240 highway permit with railroad right-of-way exception; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Serving excavation notice and notification center transmission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires excavators to serve notice by 24/7 toll-free telephone or internet 2 to 10 working days before expected excavation, and directs the notification center to identify notified participants and promptly transmit subsection 2 details to participants in the excavation area.

headings.title: Required contents of excavation notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(8), and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Lists eight required elements for notices of intent to excavate: filer/excavator contact details, start date/depth/explosives/type including trenchless excavation, excavator email/cell phone, responsible person details, accepted location description, distance/direction from roads and landmarks, site feature references, and directions to non-roadside sites.

headings.title: Optional physical or electronic white lining of excavation area
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes including Revisor footnote (*Word "sections" appears in original rolls for "section*319.024, 319.025, or 319.030"). Permits physical or available electronic white lining when subsection 2(5) means do not clearly identify the planned excavation location and preserves nonconflict with §§ 319.024, 319.025, and 319.030.

headings.title: Notification center duty to require complete notice details
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Directs the notification center to solicit and require all subsection 2 information before notice is deemed complete under §§ 319.015–319.050 and to transmit all notice details.

headings.title: Retention of notice records, recordings, and copying access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires five-year retention of notice records (including electronic records), one-year retention of telephonic recordings of original notices, and availability of copies to facility owners/operators or filing excavators for a reasonable copying fee.

headings.title: Reporting incorrect locates or unmarked facilities and corrections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires excavators discovering an incorrectly located or unmarked participant facility to notify the notification center, requires the owner to respond within two hours by contacting the excavator or correctly locating the facility, and requires correction of inaccurate location records.

headings.title: Visible markings, relocates, remarking costs, and marking limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Allows work until notice expiration while markings remain visible, requires relocate requests if work does not start within 10 working days and remarking requests if markings become unusable, requires reasonable care with potential remarking-cost liability for carelessness or repeated unnecessary requests, and restricts marking/relocating to facility owners or representatives. Independent review revised title from 'Working with visible markings, relocates, remarking, and liability' to avoid unqualified 'liability' (text says 'may be liable ... for the reasonable cost of such remarking') and cover the owner-only marking/relocating restriction.

headings.title: Pre-excavation location confirmation and hand or soft digging
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Directs excavators before digging to determine best practices for confirming horizontal and vertical facility locations based on site conditions and to use hand digging or soft digging as a best practice when possible.

headings.title: Reporting facility damage, protective devices, and 911 calls
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires reporting any excavation-related damage, dislocation, or disturbance to underground facilities or protective items (trace wires, encasements, cathode protection, permanent stakes) to the notification center, and immediate 911 contact upon a pipeline release of hazardous liquid or gas. Independent review revised title from 'Reporting facility damage, protective devices, and 911 releases' for clearer phrasing of immediate 911 contact upon a hazardous-liquid or gas pipeline release.

headings.title: No concealment, unauthorized repairs, and emergency sewer exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Prohibits concealing reportable damage/disturbance or attempting repairs without owner authorization, while allowing emergency temporary sewer repairs after notification without authorization without relieving subsection 9 reporting duties.

headings.title: Annual electric, gas, and pipeline damage data reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires electric, gas, and pipeline facility owners annually (by the Common Ground Alliance deadline) to submit prior-year damage reports to a notification-center repository as aggregated, anonymous data, with owner-specific data restricted to the submitting owner unless otherwise designated.

headings.title: Making design requests and required project information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1779, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867, A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Permits any person to submit design requests to the notification center with center-required identification, project location, and information similar to section 319.026.

headings.title: Five-working-day advance timing and center transmission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires design requests at least five working days before the requested information date and directs the notification center to identify notified participants and promptly transmit the notice to appropriate facility owners.

headings.title: Facility owner five-working-day marking or alternative agreement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires notified underground facility owners to mark locations or contact the requester within five working days, with mutually agreed alternative scheduling/methods or fallback marking within five working days if unable to agree.

headings.title: Design requests insufficient to begin excavation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Prohibits commencing excavation based on design-request information and preserves mandatory excavation notice and location duties under sections 319.025 and 319.026.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.027:57367 (all 4 subsections and L. 2008 H.B. 1779 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 5-working-day request/marking timelines, mutual-agreement fallback, and bar on starting excavation from design requests; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Two-day locate duties, status systems, meetings, and clear notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(7) (including continuation text between (6) and (7) on two telephone contact attempts), and source notes (L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 5 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Covers the two-working-day locate window starting at 12:00 a.m. (and early-start restriction), locate status system deadlines (after Dec. 31, 2014 / by Jan. 1, 2016), trenchless depth disclosure, § 319.015 markings, on-site clarification meetings, and seven methods for giving "no facilities" notice.

headings.title: Five-year retention of no-facilities notice records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires underground facility owners to record the date and means of notifying excavators that no facilities were located and retain those written records for five years.

headings.title: Excavator clarification of unclear excavation area descriptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires an excavator notified that the excavation area cannot be determined from the notice description to clarify via white flags or white paint, project plans, or an on-site meeting.

headings.title: Second no-response notice, marking deadlines, and proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires a second "no response" notice before excavating when an owner fails to comply with subsection 1, sets two-hour response and same-day/10:00 a.m. next-working-day marking deadlines (based on 2:00 p.m. cutoff), allows excavation if the owner still fails to comply, and preserves legal duties of care.

headings.title: Start time for two-working-day calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Specifies that for this section, a two-working-day period begins at 12:00 a.m. following when the request is made (echoing timing stated in subsection 1).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.030:57368 (all 5 subsections, subdivisions (1)–(7) including the unnumbered continuation paragraph between (6) and (7) on two telephone contact attempts, and L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 5 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified locate status system dates (Dec. 31, 2014 / Jan. 1, 2016), trenchless depth, on-site meetings, clear-notice methods, and 2:00 p.m. / 10:00 a.m. no-response deadlines; retained all 5 accurate titles.

headings.title: Determining sewer service connections for trenchless excavations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2014 H.B. 1867, A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Adds to section 319.030 duties by requiring a sewer system owner with facilities in the excavation area to determine whether sewer service connections exist when the notice indicates trenchless excavation methods.

headings.title: Methods for providing sewer service connection information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(4), and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Requires sewer system owners determining connections exist to provide best available location information—or notice that none exists—via a triangular green mark pointing to the customer structure, electronic copies, other agreed delivery, or an on-site meeting.

headings.title: Full compliance standard and conditional owner immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Treats providing best available information or notice of its nonexistence as full compliance with this section and shields compliant sewer system owners from liability to any party for excavation damages or injuries. Independent review revised title from 'Compliance standard and immunity from excavation liability' to make explicit that immunity is conditioned on compliance with this section.

headings.title: Providing information does not establish service-line ownership
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Clarifies that providing best available sewer service connection location information does not itself constitute ownership, operation, control, or management of sewer service lines.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.031:57369 (all 4 subsections, subdivisions (1)–(4), and L. 2014 H.B. 1867, A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified trenchless-method trigger for sewer service connections, 4 delivery methods, and non-ownership clarification; revised subsection 3 to make explicit that owner immunity is conditioned on compliance, and retained subsections 1–2 and 4.

headings.title: Obtaining information does not excuse careful excavation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 6 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). States that obtaining information required by sections 319.010 to 319.050 does not excuse any excavator from excavating in a careful and prudent manner.

headings.title: Safe-excavation duty and damage liability except section 319.034
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). States that sections 319.010 to 319.050 neither relieve an excavator of the duty to excavate safely and prudently nor absolve damage liability except as provided in section 319.034.

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption of negligence for excavator non-notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Makes an excavator's failure to give chapter-required excavation notice a rebuttable presumption of negligence if causing injury, loss, or damage, and preserves common-law liability alongside statutory penalties.

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption for owner or locator noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 133). Makes an underground facility owner's or engaged locator/contractor's failure to mark facilities under § 319.030, or an owner's failure to participate in a notification center under § 319.022, a rebuttable presumption of negligence if causing injury, loss, or damage, while preserving common-law liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.035:57371 (all 4 subsections and L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 6 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 133 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified § 319.034 exception, common-law liability preservation, and rebuttable-presumption rules for excavators, owners, and locators; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Applicability to trenchless excavation near marked facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2001 H.B. 425, A.L. 2008 H.B. 1779; Effective 1-01-09). Applies this section's procedures to trenchless excavations (including directional drilling) where underground facilities were marked under § 319.030 and any part of the intended bore walls lies within the marked approximate location.

headings.title: Location confirmation before power boring and visual-monitoring option
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2001 H.B. 425, A.L. 2008 H.B. 1779; Effective 1-01-09). Prohibits power-driven trenchless equipment within marked locations until confirming horizontal/vertical facility locations by safe noninvasive methods (barring non-owners from attaching electronic locating devices), requires periodic checks for parallel bores and monitoring of the boring device, and allows an alternative pothole visual-observation method at least two feet below the planned boring path.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.037:16986 (both subsections and L. 2001 H.B. 425, A.L. 2008 H.B. 1779 / Effective 1-01-09 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified § 319.030 marked-bore trigger, owner-only electronic locating attachment restriction, and two-foot pothole visual-monitoring alternative; retained both accurate titles.

headings.title: Civil penalties, enforcement suits, and court penalty factors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 8 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867; Effective 1-01-15). Authorizes circuit-court actions by the attorney general or a prosecuting attorney for civil penalties up to $10,000/day ($500,000 cap for a related series under §§ 319.010–319.050) for material violations of listed sections or willful facility damage, with nonjury court trial and enumerated penalty factors.

headings.title: Attorney general actions for equitable and injunctive relief
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867; Effective 1-01-15). Authorizes the attorney general to seek equitable relief—including temporary or permanent mandatory or prohibitive injunctions—in circuit court to redress or restrain violations of sections 319.010 to 319.050.

headings.title: Annual public report of aggregate enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867; Effective 1-01-15). Directs the attorney general to make public the aggregate number of enforcement actions for the prior calendar year before March 31 of the current year.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.045:16990 (all 3 subsections and L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 8 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867 / Effective 1-01-15 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified listed-section material violations, $10,000/day and $500,000 caps, AG equitable relief, and March 31 public enforcement report; retained all 3 accurate titles.

headings.title: Emergency excavation exemption and two-hour owner response
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 9 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867; Effective 1-01-15). Exempts excavations necessary due to a section 319.015 emergency from §§ 319.025 and 319.026 provided reasonable protective precautions are taken, requires substantial § 319.026 notice as soon as practical, and requires facility owners within two hours to mark, share immediate information, or advise when marking will occur.

headings.title: Notice and standard timeline for nonqualifying emergency requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867; Effective 1-01-15). Requires a facility owner receiving a nonqualifying emergency request to notify the excavator within two hours that it does not meet the § 319.015 emergency definition and will be marked within two working days under § 319.030(1).

headings.title: Potential excavator liability for nonqualifying emergency locates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867; Effective 1-01-15). States that an excavator may be liable to the owner or operator for direct locating costs associated with an emergency notification that does not meet the section 319.015 definition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.050:16992 (all 3 subsections and L. 1976 S.B. 583 § 9 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1867 / Effective 1-01-15 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified § 319.015 emergency definition cross-reference, two-hour response, nonqualifying-emergency reclassification, and permissive ('may be liable') cost liability; retained all 3 accurate titles.

headings.title: Advance notice and safety arrangements near high voltage lines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 § 4). Requires persons seeking to work temporarily closer to high voltage overhead lines than permitted under sections 319.075 to 319.090 to notify the owning/operating public utility and arrange temporary barriers, deenergization/grounding, rerouting, or conductor relocation before proceeding.

headings.title: Cost responsibility, written estimates, advance payment, and start deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 § 4). Makes the requester responsible for utility costs of temporary rerouting or conductor relocation, requires a written cost estimate upon request, excuses the utility from acting until estimated payment is made, and requires work to begin within seven working days after payment unless otherwise agreed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.083:16996 (both subsections and L. 1991 S.B. 214 & 264 § 4 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified §§ 319.075–319.090 high-voltage clearance arrangements, written estimates, advance payment, and 7-working-day start rule unless otherwise agreed; retained both accurate titles.

headings.title: Registration of tanks in service on August 28, 1989
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Required owners of existing underground storage tanks in operation (including temporarily out-of-service tanks) without prior notification to register tank age, size, type, location, and uses within 90 days after August 28, 1989.

headings.title: Registration of tanks taken out of operation 1974 to 1989
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Required owners of underground storage tanks taken out of operation between January 1, 1974, and August 28, 1989, to register tank details with the department within 90 days after August 28, 1989.

headings.title: Registration of tanks brought into use after August 28, 1989
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Requires owners bringing an underground storage tank into use after August 28, 1989, to register tank age, size, type, location, and uses within 30 days after bringing it into use.

headings.title: Exemption for tanks previously notified under federal CERCLA
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Exempts tanks notified under section 103(c) of the federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (P.L. 96-510) from subsections 1 to 3.

headings.title: Department-approved forms for tank registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Requires registrations under subsections 1 to 3 to be made on approved forms supplied by the department.

headings.title: Advance written notice and contents for permanent tank closure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6, subdivisions (1)–(5), and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Requires owners of covered tanks (including CERCLA § 103(c) and RCRA § 9002(a) tanks) permanently closed under § 319.111 to give written notice within 30 days prior to closure stating five specified items.

headings.title: Compliance deemed through federal RCRA inventory notification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Deems owners who provided underground storage tank inventory information to the department under section 9002(a) of Subtitle I of RCRA (P.L. 94-580) compliant with subsections 1 to 3.

headings.title: Depositor notice to owners on first two deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Requires persons depositing a regulated substance into an underground storage tank after August 28, 1989, upon the first two deposits, to notify the owner or operator in writing of obligations under sections 319.103 to 319.137.

headings.title: Tank seller written notice of purchaser notification duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2). Requires sellers of tanks intended for use as underground storage tanks to notify purchasers in writing of the owner's notification requirements under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.103:17001 (all 9 subsections, subdivisions (1)–(5), and L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 2 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified historical 1974/1989 registration deadlines, CERCLA § 103(c) and RCRA § 9002(a) provisions, 30-day closure notice under § 319.111, and depositor/seller notice duties; retained all 9 accurate titles.

headings.title: Department performance standards for new and upgraded tanks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 3). Directs the department to issue performance standards (covering design, construction, installation, piping, release detection, operation, and compatibility) for underground storage tanks brought into use after August 28, 1989, and for upgrading existing tanks.

headings.title: Operator duty to ensure material-substance compatibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 3). Requires the operator to ensure tank construction or lining material is compatible with the stored substance.

Verified post-Aug. 28, 1989 standards, interim installation conditions, and compatibility duty; retained all 3 accurate titles.

headings.title: Rules on financial responsibility for cleanup and third-party claims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 7, A.L. 2016 S.B. 657). Directs the department to establish rules requiring tank owners or operators to maintain financial responsibility for corrective action and third-party bodily injury and property damage from sudden and nonsudden accidental releases. Independent review revised title from 'Rules requiring financial responsibility for corrective action and injuries' to cover both third-party bodily injury and property damage rather than injuries alone.

headings.title: Acceptable forms and contractual terms of financial responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 7, A.L. 2016 S.B. 657). Lists permissible financial-responsibility mechanisms (cash trust fund, guarantee, insurance, surety/performance bond, letter of credit, self-insurance, or other department-satisfactory method) and authorizes specifying necessary or unacceptable contractual terms, conditions, or defenses.

headings.title: Cap tied to federal RCRA section 9003 amount
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 7, A.L. 2016 S.B. 657). Caps required financial responsibility at the amount required under Section 9003 of Subtitle I of the federal Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976 (P.L. 94-580), as amended.

headings.title: Guarantor liability limits and preservation of other liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 7, A.L. 2016 S.B. 657). Limits a guarantor's total section liability to its provided aggregate amount while preserving other statutory, contractual, or common-law guarantor liability (including bad faith) and preserving CERCLA §§ 107 and 111 or other applicable liability.

headings.title: Bar on incompatibility coverage denial except application fraud
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2016 S.B. 657). headings.title: Interagency inspection agreement with department of agriculture
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 8). entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.117:17007 (all 3 subsections, subdivisions (1)–(3), and L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 8 notes) and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Certificate of registration requirement and compliance condition

headings.title: Terms for initial certificates and five-year renewals

headings.title: Post-1989 department transmittal of prior notification information

headings.title: Application pathways and conditional interim tank operation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 9 subsecs. 1 to 5). entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.120:17008 (all 5 subsections and L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 9 subsecs. 1 to 5 notes) and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Grounds for denying or invalidating registration certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(2), and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 10, A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). Authorizes the department, after chapter 260 notice and hearing, to deny or invalidate a certificate issued under §§ 319.120 and 319.123 for fraudulent/deceptive registration or noncompliance with §§ 319.100–319.137 or department rules.

headings.title: Notice of hearing rights before hazardous waste commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 10, A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). Requires the department upon invalidating or refusing a certificate to advise the applicant of the right to a hearing before the hazardous waste management commission under chapter 260 procedures.

headings.title: Cleanup orders for releases posing immediate threats
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 10, A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). headings.title: Department abatement action and strict cost liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 10, A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). headings.title: Termination of insurance fund participation after appeal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 10, A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). Terminates participation in the underground storage tank insurance fund upon completion of any appeal following denial of reregistration or revocation of registration.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.125:17010 (all 5 subsections, subdivisions (1)–(2), and L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 10, A.L. 2004 S.B. 901 notes) and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Prohibited violations, compliance orders, and civil actions

headings.title: Civil penalties for order noncompliance and settlement offers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). headings.title: Constitutional disposition of recovered civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). Directs penalties recovered under this section to be handled under Article IX, Section 7 of the Missouri Constitution.

headings.title: Written compliance criteria, affirmative defense, and three-year freeze
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2004 S.B. 901). IX § 7 disposition, and 3-year compliance-criteria freeze with law-change exception; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Creation of Petroleum Storage Tank Insurance Fund trust
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 12 subsecs. 1 to 4 through A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Creates the Petroleum Storage Tank Insurance Fund as a special trust fund succeeding the underground storage tank insurance fund, excludes it from state funds, and exempts it from section 33.080 biennial transfer to general revenue.

headings.title: One-time per-tank participation fees and fund deposit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). headings.title: Treasurer deposits, security, and interest credit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Authorizes the state treasurer to deposit fund moneys in qualified state depositories secured under state-deposit laws, with earned interest credited to the fund.

headings.title: Board of trustees composition, appointments, and terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Vests fund administration and payment decisions in an 11-member board of trustees (three ex officio officials or designees plus eight senate-confirmed gubernatorial citizen appointees representing specified tank, lending, underwriting, industrial/commercial, and public-at-large sectors) serving four-year staggered terms.

headings.title: Board meeting calls, notice, consent, and quarterly minimum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Provides for calling meetings by chairman or six members with at least six days' personal or registered-mail notice, allows unanimous-consent meetings anytime, and requires at least one meeting each quarter.

headings.title: Board quorum and majority vote requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Sets six trustees as a quorum and requires a majority vote of trustees present for official board action.

headings.title: Uncompensated trustee service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Provides that trustees serve without compensation but receive actual and necessary expenses from the fund.

headings.title: Type III agency status, executive director, and board staff
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Designates the board of trustees as a type III agency authorized to appoint an executive director and state-employee staff with board-fixed salaries and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Contracted staff support from natural resources or other agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Permits the board to obtain staff resources from the department of natural resources or another state agency under negotiated cost-reimbursement contracts.

headings.title: Hiring or contracting for underwriting, claims, and defense specialists
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Authorizes the board to employ or contract with insurance underwriting, accounting, claims servicing, rate-making, and third-party defense counsel specialists serving at the board's pleasure, subject to detailed invoicing.

headings.title: Election and duties of board chairman
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Directs the board to elect a member as chairman to preside over meetings and perform board-assigned duties.

headings.title: Election and succession duties of board vice chairman
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 12 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Directs the board to elect a vice chairman to perform the chairman's duties during absence, inability, or refusal to act.

headings.title: Fiduciary rulemaking authority and cleanup-standard exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 13 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Directs the board to prescribe fiduciary management rules for §§ 319.100–319.137 while barring board oversight over environmental cleanup standards for petroleum storage tanks.

headings.title: Conflict-of-interest ban and eligible trustee claim exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 14 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Prohibits trustees and fund staff from profiting from fund moneys or transactions while preserving eligible trustees' right to submit claims or receive benefits under §§ 319.100–319.137.

headings.title: Discretionary reinsurance of fund liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 15 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Authorizes the board to reinsure all or part of the fund's liability, including at the board's option through insurers selling environmental liability insurance in Missouri.

headings.title: December 31, 2030 fund expiration and post-expiration claim wind-down
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 16 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Sets fund expiration for December 31, 2030, unless extended by the general assembly, and allows the board to continue operating afterward solely to finish paying claims made before that date.

headings.title: Annual financial audit and biennial actuarial analysis
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 17 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Requires the board to commission an annual independent financial audit and a biennial actuarial analysis of the fund, make both public, and permits contracting with third parties.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking under chapter 536 and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 18 and source notes (A.L. 2022 H.B. 2168). Directs the board to promulgate administration rules subject to chapter 536 and § 536.028 and includes a nonseverability clause invalidating rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2022, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 2011 S.B. 135). Makes board-created or board-maintained training program records public records under chapter 610 and readily available to the department of natural resources.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 2011 S.B. 135). headings.title: Elective fund participation, property transfers, and excluded sites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al. § 12 subsecs. 5 to 9 through A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). Allows tank owners/operators to participate in the fund to satisfy §§ 319.114 and 414.036, allows continued participation after property transfer under board rules, and excludes current or former refineries and petroleum pipeline or marine terminals.

headings.title: Advisory committee duties and biennial private-insurance report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). Directs the board to establish an advisory committee of insurers, tank owners/operators, and interested parties to monitor the fund, recommend changes, and report biennially to the general assembly (with the board and department of commerce and insurance) on private-market insurance viability.

headings.title: Participation applications, creditor successors, and annual payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3, subdivisions (1)–(3), and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). headings.title: Cleanup deductible, coverage caps, state-liability limits, and status reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). headings.title: Third-party injury and property coverage, caps, and exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). headings.title: Defense of eligible third-party claims and defense-cost limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). Directs the fund, in addition to other coverage limits, to defend eligible third-party claims including settlement negotiations and permits specifying a legal defense cost limit.

headings.title: Preservation of private causes of action and responsible-party liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). States that §§ 319.100–319.137 do not abrogate or limit injured persons' rights, remedies, or claims or any responsible person's liability for release-caused injury or property damage.

headings.title: Cleanup funding for participants, pre-1998 applicants, and school districts

headings.title: Legacy out-of-use underground tanks, bidding, and post-2017 owner duty

headings.title: Legacy out-of-use aboveground tanks and post-2017 owner duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10, subdivisions (1)–(2), and source notes (A.L. 2021 H.B. 604 merged with S.B. 6). headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2008 S.B. 907). Provides that no new registration fee is required for a change of ownership of a petroleum storage tank.

headings.title: Authorized site assessments and surcharges for uninsured applicants

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(4), and source notes (L. 2008 S.B. 907). headings.title: Committee report and legislative ratification of rule disapproval

headings.title: Blaster's license requirement, employer distinction, and application contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(9), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires individuals using explosives in Missouri (except subsection 18 exemptions) to hold a blaster's license, clarifies a "person using explosives" need not hold a license if all blasting is done by licensed blasters, and lists nine required application items on the division of fire safety form.

headings.title: Eligibility of qualified individuals to apply
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Permits any individual meeting subsection 4 qualifications to apply for a blaster's license.

headings.title: Application fee cap and required applicant photographs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires submitting two photographs and a rule-established application fee limited to administration costs and capped at $100.

headings.title: Qualifications required for a blaster's license
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4, subdivisions (1)–(11), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Lists 11 licensing qualifications: age 21+, no willful §§ 319.300–319.345 violations, truthful application, legal familiarity, no felony conviction/guilty plea, not a fugitive, no unlawful chapter 195 drug use, approved training/exam (except under subsecs. 11 and 13), 1,000 hours verified explosives experience within two years, not adjudicated mentally defective, and no advocacy/knowing membership in violent-action groups.

headings.title: Licensee duty to report material qualification changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires a blaster's license holder to promptly notify the division of fire safety of any change of material fact relating to any licensing qualification.

headings.title: License issuance upon finding requirements satisfied
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Directs the division of fire safety to issue a license when it finds requirements have been satisfied.

headings.title: Three-year license term and continuing training for renewal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Sets a three-year license expiration and requires eight hours of division-approved explosives training (at least half in the year before renewal), limiting carryover of excess training to no more than one subsequent renewal.

headings.title: Certificate and photo-card license documentation contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires issuing both a letter/letter-sized certificate and a ~2x3-inch photo card displaying license number, name, driver's license number, photograph, effective and expiration dates, and other needed record-keeping data.

headings.title: Carrying license documentation and enforcement exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires keeping at least one form of license documentation on the blaster's person or at the blast site and producing it upon division request, while barring enforcement action if division records document a valid license.

headings.title: License suspension or revocation grounds, surrender, and board appeal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10, subdivisions (1)–(3) and paragraphs (a)–(f), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Lists six grounds for division suspension/revocation upon substantial proof, requires certified-mail written notice (optional verbal notice) with immediate surrender and cessation of blasting, and provides a 45-day appeal to the § 319.324 state blasting safety board with a 30-day majority-vote written decision.

headings.title: Reinstatement requirements for expired blaster's licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires passing the subsection 15(1)–(5) exam and eight hours of renewal training to apply for reinstatement if expired three years or less, or meeting all subsection 4 qualifications including 20 hours of training and exam if expired more than three years.

headings.title: Licensing based on equivalent credentials from other sources
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 12 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Permits granting a license to applicants who held a valid license or certification from another source within the past three years meeting or exceeding this section's qualifications (including pre-subsection 19 rule credentials meeting rule standards), and directs the division to investigate outside qualifications. Independent review revised title from 'Reciprocal licensing based on equivalent outside credentials' to match statutory 'from any other source' rather than narrower state reciprocity.

headings.title: Employer-limited license for pre-2001 experienced blasters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 13 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Permits licensing individuals employed as blasters on or before Dec. 31, 2000, with 1,000 hours of verified training/experience for a specific employer/contractor (via affidavit) and listed subsection 4 qualifications, restricted to blasting for that affidavit-submitting person and subject to subsection 7 continuing training.

headings.title: Approved initial and renewal training courses, providers, and lists
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 14, subdivisions (1)–(4), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Requires at least two initial and two renewal courses annually by the division/agent, governs third-party course approval (3-year approval, revocable, cost-recovery fee), sets 20-hour initial and 8-hour renewal minimums, requires 10-business-day attendance reporting, and requires a public approved-provider list.

headings.title: Licensing examinations, retakes, and license renewal eligibility and fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 15, subdivisions (1)–(6), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Covers standard exams and $50 fee cap, two-year course prerequisite (except subsec. 11) and test administration, rule-set passing standards, 30-day written results, six-month retake without repeating training, and (in subdiv. (6)) renewal eligibility and matching subsection 3 renewal fee.

headings.title: Requirement of license or on-site direct supervision to load or fire
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 16 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Prohibits loading or firing explosives (or directing another to do so) without a valid blaster's license or direct supervision (supervisor physically present on the same job site), and states supervised unlicensed individuals are not in violation of §§ 319.300–319.345.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties and permanent license bar for unlicensed blasting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 17 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Makes unlicensed, unsupervised loading/firing or directing thereof a class B misdemeanor for a first offense and class A misdemeanor for a second or subsequent offense, and permanently bars individuals convicted of a class A misdemeanor under §§ 319.300–319.345 from obtaining a Missouri blaster's license.

headings.title: Exemptions from blaster's license requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 18, subdivisions (1)–(15), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Exempts 15 listed categories from blaster's licensing, including academic research/instruction, medicinal uses, official government/military operations, fireworks/flares, small arms ammunition, federally regulated underground/coal mining and industrial furnaces, equivalent federal licenses, agricultural fertilizers, transport, supervised trainees, explosives manufacturing, chapter 394 rural electric cooperatives, historic firearms/cannon, and § 256.643 agricultural irrigation well screen cleaning.

headings.title: July 2008 rulemaking deadline and initial compliance transition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 19 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). headings.title: Notices of violation and appeal procedures for subsection 6
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1286). Authorizes the state fire marshal to issue a notice of violation for subsection 6 violations subject to the procedures and appeal rights in sections 319.324, 319.327, and 319.333.

headings.title: Civil penalty caps for subsection 6 violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1286). Subjects subsection 6 violations to civil penalties not exceeding $2,000 for a first offense or $5,000 for a second or subsequent offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.318:34877 (all 8 subsections, all subdivisions/paragraphs, and L. 2007 H.B. 298, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1286 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Preserved archived cross-reference discrepancy in (5)(2) ('register or report as required by subsection 3' where annual reporting is in subsection 4), revised subsection 4 from 'mining exemption' to 'DNR-regulated exemption' for §§ 444.800–444.980 / 10 CSR 40-3.160 entities, trimmed redundant 'Prohibited' in subsection 6, and retained subsections 1–3, 5, and 7–8.

headings.title: State Blasting Safety Board creation and seven-member composition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(6), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Creates the seven-member State Blasting Safety Board within the division of fire safety, appointed by the governor with senate confirmation across listed local-government, mining (archived text reads "section 319.300 to 319.345"), construction, monitoring, manufacturing/distribution, and state fire marshal seats.

headings.title: Six-year staggered terms, reappointment, and fire marshal voting status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Sets six-year terms (staggered 1 to 6 years initially), holdover until successor naming, reappointment eligibility, and standing voting-member status for the state fire marshal or designee.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement, meeting sites, and agreed conference-call hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 (including continuation paragraph) and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Provides uncompensated service with division expense reimbursement, division-arranged meeting facilities, agreed Missouri hearing locations, and conference-call hearings upon agreement of the licensee, state fire marshal, and board chairman.

headings.title: Annual election and presiding duties of board chairman
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Directs the board annually by January 31 to elect by majority vote a chairman (other than the state fire marshal or designee) to preside over meetings and hearings and perform §§ 319.300–319.345 duties.

headings.title: State fire marshal or designee as board secretary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Assigns the duties of board secretary to the state fire marshal or designee.

headings.title: Calling meetings and annual meeting minimum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Provides for calling board meetings by the chairman or written notice of the state fire marshal and requires at least one meeting each calendar year.

headings.title: Advisory, exam-approval, appeal-hearing, and rule-approval duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7, subdivisions (1)–(5), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Directs the board to advise on forms/training/exams/fees, approve or disapprove blaster exams, hear and decide by majority vote appeals under §§ 319.306(10), 319.318(7), and 319.333, approve or disapprove proposed division rules, and assist in §§ 319.300–319.345 administration/enforcement.

headings.title: Board majority vote required for enforcement referrals after hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Restricts the state fire marshal from referring notices of violation or requesting criminal/civil enforcement or injunctive relief for matters heard under subsection 7(3) without a majority vote of the board.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.324:17034 (all 8 subsections, all subdivisions, subsection 3 continuation paragraph on agreed conference-call hearings, and L. 2007 H.B. 298 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified archived singular 'section 319.300 to 319.345' in (1)(2), fire marshal voting/secretary roles, and majority-vote referral gate in subsection 8; retained all 8 accurate titles.

headings.title: Division duties for forms, exams, rules, investigations, and cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(5) and paragraphs (a)–(e), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Assigns the division of fire safety duties for forms/certificates, blaster exams, board-approved rulemaking not conflicting with listed federal laws/agencies, complaint/cause investigations by blaster-qualified division inspectors (note archived subdiv. (4) refers to "registration and reporting records required by section 319.315" though registration/annual reporting is in § 319.318), and intergovernmental cooperation.

headings.title: Enforcement referrals, civil penalty caps, and board-vote gate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Authorizes referrals to the attorney general or prosecuting attorneys for criminal, civil, or injunctive relief, sets civil penalties up to $2,000 first / $5,000 subsequent offense for §§ 319.300–319.345 violations (excluding § 319.306(16) violations), and requires a board majority vote before referring matters heard under § 319.324(7)(3).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.327:17035 (both subsections, subdivisions (1)–(5), paragraphs (a)–(e), and L. 2007 H.B. 298 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Preserved without altering the archived cross-reference discrepancy in (1)(4) ('registration and reporting records required by section 319.315' although registration/annual reporting appears in § 319.318), verified federal non-conflict list, § 319.306(16) penalty exclusion, and § 319.324(7)(3) board-vote referral gate; retained both accurate titles.

headings.title: Two-business-day advance notice to division for new blast sites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Requires notifying the division of fire safety in writing or by phone at least two business days before first using explosives at a new site, with only one advance notice required for ongoing projects or permanent sites such as mines.

headings.title: Required information in division pre-blasting notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Requires the notice to state the explosives user's name, address, and phone number, supervising individual's name, date or approximate period, location description, and project nature or reason for blasting.

headings.title: Exemption for state, federal, or political subdivision contract blasting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Exempts blasting required by a contract with any Missouri state agency, federal agency, or political subdivision from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.339:17039 (all 3 subsections and L. 2007 H.B. 298 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 2-business-day new-site advance notice, single-notice rule for ongoing/permanent sites, required contents, and public-contract exemption; retained all 3 accurate titles.

headings.title: Advance blasting notice to municipalities and fire protection officials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Requires two-business-day advance notice to municipal representatives for municipal blasting and to fire protection officials everywhere, specifies notice contents, requires one notice for ongoing/permanent sites, and exempts ongoing or permanent sites existing on August 28, 2007.

headings.title: Pre-blasting notice to nearby residences and businesses in municipalities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Requires municipal blasters to notify owners or occupants of residences or businesses within a scaled distance of 55 before blasting at a new location via one listed method, and permits municipalities to furnish owner/occupant contact data upon request.

headings.title: Authorized municipal and county blasting permit ordinances and terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3, subdivisions (1)–(8), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Authorizes municipal or county ordinances/orders covering permits (due <=10 days ahead), explosive/storage details, street signage/traffic plans, blasting hours (>=8 consecutive hours, Sunday ban unless approved), proof of registration/licensure, $1M–$5M liability insurance, three attempts for preblast surveys within scaled distance 35 (with owner consent), and suspension/revocation/fines.

headings.title: Issuance of local blasting permits and administrative fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Directs municipalities or counties to grant blasting permits under subsection 3 ordinances upon meeting ordinance requirements and paying a reasonable administrative fee.

headings.title: Local inspection, observation, record review, and reporting powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5, subdivisions (1)–(4), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Authorizes municipal, county, or fire protection officials to inspect registration/§ 319.306 license proof, observe blasting from a blaster-designated safe spot, examine §§ 319.309/319.315 records (without requiring surrender except for local permit-violation investigations), and report suspected §§ 319.300–319.345 violations (archived text reads "section 319.300 to 319.345") to the division.

headings.title: Preemption bar on conflicting local rules and charter-county exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6, subdivisions (1)–(5), and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Bars existing (as of Aug. 28, 2007) or future municipal or county ordinances/orders from preempting, amending, exceeding, or conflicting with §§ 319.300–319.342, § 319.327 rules, or five listed federal authorities, while excepting charter counties with more than one million inhabitants.

headings.title: Public-agency construction contract exemption from subsections 1 to 3
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). Exempts blasting required by a construction contract with any state agency, federal agency, or political subdivision from subsections 1, 2, and 3. Independent review revised title from 'Exemption for public-agency construction contracts' to preserve the explicit limitation of the exemption to subsections 1, 2, and 3.

headings.title: Preservation of statutory and common-law remedies for blast damage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (L. 2007 H.B. 298). States that nothing in this section preempts statutory or common-law rights and remedies of persons damaged by blasting.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.342:17040 (all 8 subsections, all subdivisions, and L. 2007 H.B. 298 notes) and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Periodic reporting duty for hazardous-liquid pipeline owners and operators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 45 § 1). Requires owners or operators of pipelines transporting hazardous liquids as defined in the federal Hazardous Liquid Pipeline Safety Act of 1979 (49 U.S.C. 2001, et seq.) to submit periodic reports required by the director of natural resources under this section. Independent review noted archived text cites the 'federal Hazardous Liquid Pipeline Safety Act of 1979, 49 U.S.C. 2001, et seq.' in contrast to section 319.503(1), which omits 'Hazardous.'

headings.title: Categories of pipeline and emergency-plan information director may require
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(8) and paragraphs (a)–(c), and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 45 § 1). Lists eight categories the director may require in periodic reports: contact/emergency phone, facility maps, pipeline characteristics, transported products, operations/maintenance manual, release emergency response plan (discovery actions, agency liaison, immediate notification), latest test results, and other useful/necessary information.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 319.500:17043 (both subsections, subdivisions (1)–(8), paragraphs (a)–(c), and L. 1991 S.B. 45 § 1 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified exact federal statute citation 'Hazardous Liquid Pipeline Safety Act of 1979, 49 U.S.C. 2001, et seq.' (contrasted with § 319.503(1)'s omission of 'Hazardous') and all 8 discretionary reporting categories; retained both accurate titles.

headings.title: Civil actions, penalties, water-quality factors, venue, and fund deposit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 45 § 2). Authorizes the DNR director (via AG or prosecutor) to sue owners/operators of hazardous-liquid pipelines (archived text cites "federal Liquid Pipeline Safety Act of 1979, 49 U.S.C. 2001, et seq.") responsible for a hazardous substance emergency for injunctions, up to $10,000/day emergency penalties, and up to $2,500/day ($500,000 cap) chapter 644 water-quality penalties with judicial factors, venue rules, and deposit of non-Article IX, Section 7 moneys into the § 640.220 natural resources protection fund.

headings.title: Bar on duplicate administrative penalties and habitual-violator exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 45 § 2). Precludes administrative penalties for the same violation once a civil-penalty suit is commenced, except for department-determined habitual violators of Missouri, other-state, or federal clean water laws, and directs the commission to adopt rules clarifying "habitual violator."

headings.title: Affirmative defenses to pipeline emergency liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1991 S.B. 45 § 2). Relieves a person otherwise liable under §§ 319.500 and 319.503 upon demonstrating the hazardous substance emergency resulted from an act of God, act of war, act of Missouri or the United States, or solely the act of a third party.
